answer_1.quote: The goal of this paper is to present a theoretically grounded framework to mitigate bias in dialogue systems.
answer_1.outputs: generated dialogues in a visual dialogue game where a question-player asks yes/no questions to identify a goal object

answer_2.quote: To evaluate human likeness, we use metrics proposed by : average accuracy acc in identifying the true goal-object across three random seeds, average lexical diversity (ldiv; type/token ratio over all dialogues), average question diversity (qdiv; % unique questions over all dialogues), and average percent of dialogues with repeated questions (repq).

answer_4.quote: hum.eval. is % of model dialogues using gendered words correctly based on annotation (50 per method per annotator). Namely, two annotators were asked to determine correctness of gendered word use, evaluating both incorrect usage as well as false negatives; i.e., where use would be appropriate/helpful.
answer_4.guideline: determine correctness of gendered word use, evaluating both incorrect usage as well as false negatives; i.e., where use would be appropriate/helpful
